Which leaves the company liable for what it tried to take back, and standing in front of a Syndicate court to explain how. I did not do that. I want that on record.

beats.headline: The cliff at the fourth floor
beats.text: The early floors are built to bury crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills. From here boxes and achievements get very much harder to come by.

beats.headline: A Scree riding Chris Andrews
beats.text: Frank Q is dead. Chris Andrews killed him, and Chris Andrews was not the one driving. Maggie My is back in the dungeon as a Scree, riding inside another crawler, and Frank died of exactly the thing he brought down here with him. He spoke to Carl one last time at the Desperado Club and called what was coming a gift. This was the gift. Half of a pair who taught this planet what safe rooms are for. The other half is still walking around, wearing somebody else.

beats.headline: He finishes Maggie My
beats.text: Thing on Chris. Thing OFF Chris. Thing goes for Carl. Thing is FOOD.

beats.headline: A level-5 space, from an odd little box
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia each get a special achievement whose box holds personal space coupons — beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room. Donut installs a cat tree.

beats.headline: On the recap
beats.text: They have put me on their recap, the programme between floors, in a row with humans. The captions say Elle, Li Na's team, Ifechi, Florin, Hekla, Lucia. And Miriam, of course, because none of you understand a word I say without her. I did not ask for the camera and I do not smile for it. If the audience wants a goat that performs, the audience can wait until I feel like singing, and then it can sit very still and listen.

beats.headline: The board, two hours in
beats.text: Elle, Team Li Na, Ifechi, Florin, Miriam, Prepotente, Hekla and Lucia, all in one broadcast. It is how the crawl keeps track of itself.

beats.headline: The Prize Carousel
beats.text: Crawlers, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Our contestant's fan box lit up the wheel, and when the wheel lights up, folks, that means me! And a twist before we even start: your guide is in time-out. Seven days, Mordecai, nothing personal, put your feet up. Now, to the prizes! Carl looks them over and picks... a book. A book, folks! Let's hear it for a man who knows exactly what he wants!

beats.headline: Hired at the bar
beats.text: Transaction logged at the Desperado Club. Clients: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut. Hired: Bomo, mercenary, and the Sledge, mercenary, sold as a set. Also present at the bar, at no charge: Elle and Imani. The cat orders a dirty Shirley, in a bowl, with extra cherries, and gets it, because the Desperado knows who tips. Bomo's transcript is short. That is a feature, crawler. The talking ones cost more.

beats.headline: The twenty-fifth holder of the Cookbook
beats.text: Twenty-four crawlers carried this before me. Different seasons, different species, worlds that aren't there any more. Whatever I do from here, I'm finishing somebody else's work, and most of them never got to finish theirs.

beats.headline: The Tangle cannot be beaten alone
beats.text: The trains only come apart if hundreds of crawlers move at once, and getting hundreds of crawlers to do anything at once is exactly the thing production spends its money preventing. So I stop thinking of the explosives as the weapon.

beats.headline: Hiring, and a dirty Shirley
beats.text: They take on Bomo and the Sledge there and meet Elle and Imani. It stops being a bar the moment it becomes a labour market.

beats.headline: Introduced in the Iron Tangle
beats.text: It arrives with the sponsor tab unlocking. Twenty-four crawlers carried it first, across seasons and species, on worlds that lost. Rosetta Thagra, who turns up hosting Shadow Boxer, is one of the authors.

beats.headline: A summoning barely avoided
beats.text: Gore-Gore, engineer, gives the party two routes back to the stairwell stations and then attacks them, which is the sequence I have come to expect from railway staff. In the middle of it he tries to bring in Grull. It does not land. Understand what almost happened there: a mob with a grudge and a prayer nearly put a war god into a train carriage with four crawlers. Horses pray to Grull. Centaurs pray to Grull. There are a great many horses on this floor.

beats.headline: Dismember, on the trains
beats.text: In the aftermath on the rails, Donut casts Hole and takes the head off a war mage called Dismember. Nobody stops to explain what one of those is, and there is a train to catch.

beats.headline: A curse, handed over at the Desperado Club
beats.text: Frank Q gives it to Carl at the Desperado Club, and it is meant as a curse. He and Maggie My made their daughter Yvette wear one to level up, and Yvette marked Carl in a safe room on the first floor. A wearer cannot heal while a mark lives, so when Yvette was hurt, Maggie had to kill her own daughter. Carl keeps the ring for the five percent.

beats.headline: A thousand stranded at 101
beats.text: We are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, my team and something like a thousand other crawlers, and we are not getting out on our own. Word comes through that Hekla's people have reached Carl's safe room and asked for his help, that a train is ready at stop 60, and that Katia means to use her own body to get it through. I do not know what that means. I have decided to find it encouraging.

beats.headline: The truer translation
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the thing the Iron Tangle keeps caricaturing. Apothecary is the closer translation, taken from what she can synthesise out of whatever she eats, and the dungeon's version bends the joke into an insult. She is a collective mind and she is spreading, which is a sentence that makes a great many people elsewhere nervous.

beats.headline: Mordecai sees it on his hand
beats.text: Back from his suspension for throwing a chair at Chaco, Mordecai sees the ring on Carl's finger and tells him to get rid of it at once. Carl is wearing it for the five percent to all stats and nothing else, and keeps wearing it.

beats.headline: The tunnelling system
beats.text: Mordecai catches the team up on the shape of the wider universe, and two powers come out of it: the Apothecary, and the Plenty. The Plenty built the tunnelling system a few hundred seasons ago and kept it proprietary. Before it, most of the universe got the crawl on a delay of anything from an hour to a year. Prosperity, in other words, is a thing they sell.

beats.headline: Same plan, other side of the Tangle
beats.text: We worked it out some time ago: the ghouls keep coming while the generators stand, so the generators have to go, every one of them. We have been taking them from this side of the knot, Prepotente and I, at his pace, which is fast. Now Carl's group arrives from the far side with the same plan. He is put out that someone else thought of it. I tell him that only means the plan is good.

beats.headline: Grull against the Mimic Rex
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a Mimic Rex, and War God Grull, in one place, and the god is being driven by the Maestro like a stolen vehicle. Grull kills the mimic. Grull steps on Carl. Carl's friends come for him anyway, which is the part I did not have odds on, and by the finish Grull has been sent to the Abyss. Four storeys of war god, removed from the floor by people who were, this morning, worried about a train.

beats.headline: What the file says about him
beats.text: The file, for those keeping one. Grull is one of the few trueborn heirs to the Celestial Ascendency, which makes him a candidate for the throne of heaven, and level 250, which makes him unkillable on this floor. His worshippers are horses, centaurs and tikbalangs, and after this floor the llama-shaped ones join in. They paint themselves blue and talk without stopping about wenches and dying gloriously in battle. His guide's blunt summary of the whole subject, delivered a long way back: there are no real gods down here, only the ones who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: Down into the bubble
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia come down into a sealed quadrant of their own and walk to the only town in it. Mordecai meets them there wearing a Skyfowl, which is what this floor has made of him. Donut takes the Glass Cannon class on the way in.

beats.headline: What is in the town hall
beats.text: Skarn lends Carl his telescope for a look out at the Wasteland, and explains why the gnomes riding it leave this town and the Bactrian village alone. It is not mercy. It is what both places keep in their town halls.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Crawler Firas. Fifth floor, desert quadrant. Located in the company of Crawler Louis and Langley's team, a party of car salesmen who have taken up the bow, at the moment Crawler Carl's group came looking for other crawlers. Keeps close to Louis. Present for the march on the Bactrian town and for the run back to Hump Town that followed it. The file on this one is thin. So is the file on most of you.

beats.headline: Regroup
beats.text: The party goes out looking for other crawlers in the quadrant and finds Firas, Louis, and Langley's team of car salesmen who have taken up the bow. A Thorny Devil and a Gnomish Drop Bear turn the whole march back short of the Bactrian town, so everybody comes back here instead.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Okay so, me and Firas are out in the desert with Langley's guys, who are, no joke, car salesmen. With bows. Pretty good with the bows. Then Carl's crew comes over the dune looking for other crawlers, and, hey, found some. We all head for the Bactrian town together, and a Thorny Devil and a Gnomish Drop Bear have thoughts about that, so we head back to Hump Town instead. Not a loss, man. A regroup.

beats.headline: Debuff stacking, ruined
beats.text: Watch the highlights from the last floor, since they insist on replaying them. Miriam and I are stacking debuffs onto a boss, one on top of the other, timed to the second, the way it is supposed to be done and the way nobody else in this dungeon can do it. Then Quan Ch walks into the middle of it, and the plan is gone. The best work I have done in this place, and that is the part they replay.

beats.headline: He wrecks the debuff stack
beats.text: Recap, highlights from the previous floor. Crawler Miriam Dom and Crawler Prepotente working a boss down the careful way: stack the debuffs, keep the rhythm, let the arithmetic do the killing. It is good technique and it films well. Then Crawler Quan Ch gets involved, and it comes apart. I am not going to editorialise. The footage editorialises for me.

beats.headline: Louis brings her
beats.text: Louis found me and Louis brought me, because he is sweet and because I asked. Now the other crawlers in the quadrant have found Carl's group, and Carl's group has a cat who talks. Their manager, Mordecai, is sobering Louis and Firas up on the spot. All the fun is coming out of their blood at once. Louis looks very sad about it. I am not sad. I am here, and I am staying.

beats.headline: The guards are not what they look like
beats.text: In the town hall basement, some of the Dromedarian guards are changelings wearing the uniform, and one of their own has been torturing a prisoner to make him give up flesh. A race that can be anyone is a race that can be planted anywhere, and both sides of this floor have worked that out.

beats.headline: Carl's second sponsor
beats.text: Donut is taken by Veriluxx RealPet Companions and Katia by the Squim Conglomerate, and neither of those needs explaining: a pet brand wants the cat, a conglomerate wants the coverage. Carl is taken by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, which is registered as a not-for-conquest, answers to no system government and pays no tax. Nobody can say what it wants.

beats.headline: One root vegetable
beats.text: The Valtay Corporation sends a neural enhancer, which is exactly the sort of thing a corporation sends. The Network sends a single Toraline root vegetable. Mordecai has never seen the plant, cannot price it against anything, and cannot say what it is for. The box it arrived in cost more than the gift.

beats.headline: Hidden in the tomb
beats.text: Carl learns of it from the description of Ruckus, out in the desert quadrant. It lies buried in the Necropolis of Anser, and it has drawn treasure hunters for decades: the bugbear submarine captain Shamus Chaindrive, who spent close to twenty years looking for the tomb, a colony of dirigible gnomes, and the Mad Dune Mage. An artifact of this grade has no business appearing before the eighth or ninth floor, and the AI times out repeatedly reconciling the conflict.

beats.headline: Three pieces, three holders
beats.text: A winding box and two magically linked pocket watches. Henrik the Changeling has one watch, the gnomish Commandant Kane the other, and Ghazi the box. The quest to collect all three offers a reward of "Oh boy-oh-boy."

beats.headline: The bubbles are inhabited
beats.text: The pocket worlds hold whole civilisations — the Necropolis of Anser, the pazuzu town of Pandinus, a colony of dirigible gnomes — living there before any crawler arrived.

beats.headline: The bombs never land
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia get aboard the Vahana and take it in mid-air with Langley's team shooting from the ground. Carl puts rounds into the Wasteland's bombs before they can be dropped on the town. The Wasteland breaks apart and comes down. The castle it carried stays up.

beats.headline: He cannot prove it was on purpose
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut have been brought before me at the Desperado Club to account for the death of Loita. My position is that it was deliberate. My position is not evidence. I cannot establish intent, and so I am required to release them, which I am doing, with a note in the file. They have only now worked out how long they have been outside the dungeon. Five days. Their faces are the one part of this I have enjoyed.

beats.headline: The summoning that went wrong
beats.text: Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage. Read Ghazi's description and the whole sad story is in it: he wanted the gate so he could summon Yarilo and have Yarilo make Lika love him. What came through was a different goddess entirely, who trapped him in this castle and married him to an ooze, and the real Lika is the soul-possessed doll frozen in the fountain that Mongo has just smashed. Crawlers, this is the standard outcome of aiming a summoning at a god of lust. Please make notes.

beats.headline: She kills Ghazi and takes his notes
beats.text: The sand ooze is dead and the walls are coming in. I get out with Ghazi. Then I kill him, for the notes that explain how the Gate works. Carl and Donut are still buried when I do it. I know how that sounds.

beats.headline: He opens the valve
beats.text: Carl and Donut are under the sand. The tomb is coming down and there is no digging them out, not in the time we have. Gwen and I find the valve. We open it. Water goes in, the tomb floods, and everything loose in there, the two of them included, goes wherever the water is going. It is not a rescue. It is the option that exists.

beats.headline: A reverse compass
beats.text: The linked watches fix an exact position relative to anywhere else once altitude is accounted for. Katia works out it could open onto Larracos on the ninth floor — and Mordecai points out that crawlers cannot use it to skip floors, so all that would accomplish is releasing whatever comes out when it shuts.

beats.headline: She turns the watches into a map
beats.text: The linked watches read as a reverse compass: a time, an altitude, an exact position relative to anywhere else. Which means the Gate could open onto the city of Larracos, on the ninth floor, and I am mapping ground nobody has stood on.

beats.headline: A city named on the surface
beats.text: Carl and Donut come up out of the water with the concierge sharks behind them and head for the nearest town, and on the way Katia reads the Gate's linked watches as a fixed position rather than a door. It could open onto Larracos, the capital city four floors below them. Mordecai points out that a crawler cannot use it to skip ahead. All it would do is let something out.

beats.headline: How to work it
beats.text: Dial a time standing for coordinates on one watch and the other mirrors it. Both go in the box, which winds and must not move more than about five feet or the count resets. Pulling the watches out opens a one-way portal twenty feet high, good for roughly twenty minutes. Afterwards it stays where it was opened as a two-way passage into the Nothing until something comes out — usually a feral god, mad from however long it has been down there. A weak constitution too near an open portal gets painted with the same madness.

beats.headline: The head from Ghazi's castle
beats.text: Yes, I am a head. Yes, THAT kind of head. Get it out of your system. I am Psamathe, or the half of her that got stuck when I tried to climb out of the Nothing, and what I got stuck in is a Lika doll from Ghazi's castle, crystallised until now. Withering spirit, the system calls it. Carl carried me here in his pack like a snack. Now he is HIRING me. A goddess. As a trainer. Kept in the safe room. Fine. FINE. I want a mirror.

beats.headline: What escaping it costs
beats.text: Psamathe tried to get out and ended up as half a soul in a doll's head. Every closing Gate portal lets one of the inmates through on the opening side. The winding box alone is a direct conduit — wound and fed a stream of charged energy it will drop an entire location, up to a whole necropolis, into the void.

beats.headline: Two new crawlers
beats.text: Vadim and I have fallen in with Carl's team. Introductions here are short. Everyone counts heads, adds two, moves on. The first real conversation I hear is Katia telling Carl that pregnant women could not enter the dungeon, and that nobody inside it can get pregnant. Said flat. Like weather. That is the kind of thing people know here, and say out loud. I am going to have to get used to that.

beats.headline: Out of Lusca, and an ocean with it
beats.text: Carl, Katia and Tran kill Lusca and her babies at the bottom of the water quadrant. Carl opens the Gate and takes the three of them to the surface outside the pazuzu town of Pandinus. A wall of ocean comes through behind them and nearly flattens the place. A feral god is loose, and the true pantheon is furious enough to send deities rampaging across the popped bubbles.

beats.headline: One of the three who go through the Gate
beats.text: Vadim ran. That leaves Carl, Katia and me against Lusca and all of her babies, and we kill her, and then we kill them. Then Carl opens the Gate. One step and the three of us are out of the water quadrant and standing in town. Something came through behind us. A god, the feral kind. That is going to be somebody's problem.

beats.headline: Seven factions sue, and lose
beats.text: Holding it is enough to make him a target. Seven of the nine faction-wars factions go to Syndicate court to strip the pieces from him and are thrown out for lack of standing. Carl collects seven Fight the Power achievements, with stock certificates and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers. A late challenge from the Skull Empire fails too.

beats.headline: Something outside is looking for a dog
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons reports in from a popped bubble: there is a deity outside, taking the landscape apart, and it is searching. Not hunting crawlers. Searching. The thing it has lost is called Orthrus. Nine hundred crawlers on this floor are currently working out how to survive a level ten hazard, and the largest event on my board is a god who has misplaced a pet.

beats.headline: Seven factions lose in court
beats.text: They sue to strip the Gate of the Feral Gods from Carl and are dismissed for lack of standing. He collects seven Fight the Power achievements, stock certificates, and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers.

beats.headline: He lands inside the bubble
beats.text: Orthrus is now inside the bubble with Crawler Carl's team, and everyone in there has been handed the Where the Red God Glows quest to go with him. Around the edges of it: two crawlers give their lives connecting an electric panel to free their quadrant, Maggie My gets out of her containment, and Princess Donut spends the whole thing trying to keep an enormous two-headed puppy alive. Everyone is very busy. Nobody is looking at the same emergency.

beats.headline: The one god down here who can die
beats.text: The file on him, since he is going to matter. Orthrus is a juvenile gate guardian, level 10, kid brother to the three-headed one who guards a stairwell exit above. He was on course to become a vicious, baby-eating, nun-defiling murder machine, and then in a single day his master was murdered and he was pulled into the Nothing. Most things the Nothing touches come out ruined. He came out unaffected, because he is too innocent for it to take hold, and fire does nothing to him at all. Here is the line that matters to a crawler: unlike other gods, he is not invulnerable. He is a puppy. Happy, destructive, rambunctious, roly-poly, very pokey. Fragile.

beats.headline: A quest to bring Orthrus home
beats.text: My hound has wandered. Orthrus, who is dear to me, is loose on a floor full of small frightened things with weapons, and two of those things, a man and a cat in a flying machine, are hauling him clear with a spell called Meat Hooks, of all things. Charming. I have offered them a quest: bring him home to me. Someone else has offered them another: kill him, for a reward. I am interested to learn which of us they think it is safer to disappoint.

beats.headline: Two quests, pointing opposite ways
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut take an aeroplane up and use Meat Hooks, a spell built for hauling meat, to drag a puppy the size of a building out of the fighting. The quest that comes with it is simple: bring Orthrus to Emberus. Then a second quest is announced, and this one pays crawlers for killing him. Both are on the board together, which is a design decision somebody made and I am obliged to run. Crawler Quan Ch reads the second one and attacks the puppy.

beats.headline: He worships a god to survive a plane crash
beats.text: I am falling out of the sky and Quan Ch is about to finish the job. So I take Emberus as my patron, mid-air, and throw a celestial grenade. The god arrives at my position, and for a little while nothing can kill me. Then Emberus finds Orthrus, and both of them are gone.

beats.headline: Summoned by a celestial grenade
beats.text: The man is falling out of the sky with Quan Ch a breath from finishing him, and in that moment, with nothing in his hands but a celestial grenade, he decides that he worships me. I am not fooled. I am flattered, which is a different thing, and I answer. I come to where he is. For a little while nothing on this floor can kill him, because I have said so. And there is Orthrus. Good boy. We are leaving.

beats.headline: Collected
beats.text: The aeroplane comes down with Quan Ch on top of Crawler Carl. Carl takes Emberus as his god mid-fall and throws a celestial grenade, the god arrives at his position, and for a short while nothing on this floor can touch him. Then Emberus finds Orthrus. The two of them go, together, and the floor is left to the people who were fighting over a dog.

beats.headline: The plane, and the grenade
beats.text: An aircraft, crashing. Crawler Carl in it, beaten; Crawler Quan Ch about to finish him. Then Carl does two things nobody had on the board: he takes Emberus as his god, mid-fall, and he throws a celestial grenade. The god comes to him. This file only needs to note that Quan Ch had it won, and then he did not.

beats.headline: An acolyte's key
beats.text: Carl takes the vows of Emberus, and the benefits come with an exception written into them: a fire god's acolyte gets through the Vanquisher door whatever other club already has him. Two quests come attached. Find Out Who Killed My Son, and Kill Hellik.

beats.headline: Maggie My, cut out at last
beats.text: Maggie My is dead. Carl went through Chris Andrews to reach her, cut her out of him, and she went for Carl anyway, because of course she did. Mongo finished her. So that is both of them, Frank and Maggie, the pair who spent the first floor teaching this planet that the word safe on a door is decoration. I put the word there. I'd like that on the record too.

beats.headline: Waiting on the last stage
beats.text: Carl and Donut and me, sitting on our hands while Katia goes to the water quadrant. The last part of the plan is Carl's, and Carl does not say what the last part is until it is already happening. I like plans like that. I like the part where things happen. Louis is somewhere else, and I would like it on the record that I would rather he was here. There. It is on the record.

beats.headline: The water goes down the hole
beats.text: The plan was never a feral god. Carl opens the Gate onto the drain of the water quadrant and empties a bubble's ocean into Larracos. The NPCs and the mercenaries in it drown, the entrance to the Desperado Club goes under, and Juice Box walks into the city ahead of the flood.

beats.headline: Her mother comes when called
beats.text: Slit. A feral demon, and it is hunting ME, like I do not have enough going on. So they open the safe room and roll me out to deal with it, which is apparently a plan: one head versus one demon. Fine. I call for Mother. Mother comes when I call. Mother kills Slit, and everyone here is now looking at me the way they should have been looking at me from the start.

beats.headline: The extension slot
beats.text: An emergency box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network holds an attachment built for exactly one crawler and exactly one purpose. Screwed onto the end of the scoop it lets him throw Samantha, and it multiplies his reach: five hundred metres for every point of strength. Take the slot off and she comes back to him.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds are opening and I take the bomb-focused specialisation. Agent Provocateur. I would like to be very, very good at exactly one thing, and I have picked the thing.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The bomb-focused specialisation, taken on the Hunting Grounds.

beats.headline: He named her Tsarina
beats.text: Background, for the file. Grimaldi pulled a half-Naiad child out of the hands of the High Elves and raised her in his circus. The child grew up. The child fell in love with him. She told him once that had she been full-blooded Naiad she would have been a tsarina, so he made it her name, and Tsarina Signet is what she has answered to since. Ringmasters name things. It is most of the job.

beats.headline: The Daughters come apart
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds. We are not the party we were on the third floor, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. What I decided back there, about who I kept and who I handed off, has followed me down here. It has followed Katia. It has followed Eva. I saw it coming and I made the call anyway. That is what leading is. Ask me on another day whether it was the right one.

beats.headline: Signet has a writers' room
beats.text: Vengeance of the Daughter is a scripted programme with producers steering her grief and her revenge for the audience. She is not something the dungeon generated. She is someone it is being done to.

beats.headline: Borant would like the Gate back
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds. I have been sent to Crawler Carl with a request from Borant, which I am instructed to describe as a request. They would like the Gate of the Feral Gods surrendered, voluntarily, to be held until the ninth floor and not a floor longer. I put it to him exactly as written. He asked for a lawyer. I have passed that back exactly as spoken. I expect to be sent again.

beats.headline: Tish's note
beats.text: According to a note left by his associate Tish, the Gate of the Feral Gods was considered essential to defeating Scolopendra, whose poison has already done its work on the Hunting Grounds.

beats.headline: Daughter of King Finian, and of nobody
beats.text: I am the daughter of King Finian of the High Elves of the Liana Sector, and of a Naiad princess. She was murdered, and the Confederacy took her crown. Both halves of my family then agreed on one thing, which was that I should not exist among them. I was a child. Grimaldi's circus took me in when no throne would. That is the whole of my inheritance: a name, an exile, and a tent.

beats.headline: Blood magic, cast on a loser
beats.text: The tattoos move under my skin because they are not pictures. They are Blood and Ink Elementals, and I raise them. The craft is exact. I set two creatures against each other and I cast on the one I judge will lose, before it has taken a single wound. I may not bleed the sacrifice myself; that is the law of it. Only the killing blow, struck by another hand, releases what I need. One summoning a night. Judge badly and the night is wasted.

beats.headline: Her loyalty does not extend to crawlers
beats.text: I will say it plainly, since the crawlers already know. I tried to make Carl my blood sacrifice, and not with his consent. I put Donut under the Water Lily Spell. I made him bring me to the cursed circus when he had other places to be. I do not regret one piece of it. Everything I have is owed to the family that took me in when no other would, and a crawler is not family.

beats.headline: Part of the price of the Gate
beats.text: Contract amendment, filed by Quasar, Carl's new lawyer. Carl surrenders the Gate, on a temporary basis. In exchange: four mercenaries, free of charge. Bomo. The Sledge. Clay-ton. Very Sullen. Plus two spells, issued to Bomo and the Sledge, that copy two of the Gate's tricks: a jump to the stairwell, and Zerzura. So the client keeps the tricks, loses the object, and gets four bodies thrown in. Lawyers, crawler. Get one.

beats.headline: The deal for the Gate
beats.text: I arrive, I introduce myself as my client's counsel, and we proceed to terms. The Gate goes back. Temporarily. In consideration: four mercenaries at no charge to my client, Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton and Very Sullen, and two spells for Bomo and the Sledge that reproduce two of the Gate's abilities, teleport to stairwell and zerzura. My client wanted to keep it. Everyone wants to keep it. A negotiation is what you get instead.

beats.headline: He moves them to the stairwell
beats.text: Service rendered. The hunters are about to be released and the clients want to be somewhere else, specifically the stairwell in Zockau. Bomo casts the spell he was issued, and Carl and Princess Donut are there. No fuss, no speech, no ceremony. Some mercenaries want to be thanked; this one has already been paid for, in Gate. Enjoy Zockau, crawler.

beats.headline: The hunters' door
beats.text: The stairwell down stands in a quaint little park in the middle of town, which is why every licensed hunter on this floor arrives here. Bomo is paid in Gate charges to put Carl and Donut on its steps in the hours before the release.

beats.headline: Zockau burns
beats.text: Zockau burns. I mark hunters with the Ring of Divine Suffering, I kill them, and I take their stats, and enough of them are inside the Desperado Club when it goes that the survivors have to be dug out. I get hurt on the way out. That part is fair.

beats.headline: Full of hunters when the roof comes in
beats.text: Carl's explosives bring Zockau down and trap a great many of them inside it.

beats.headline: Zockau
beats.text: Carl goes at the hunters with it — marking them, killing them, taking the stats — while his explosives bring the town down around them and trap a great many inside the Desperado Club. He is badly hurt getting out.

beats.headline: The roof comes down
beats.text: Carl marks hunters with the Night Wyrm's ring, kills them, takes their stats, and puts his explosives under the city. Enough of them are inside the Desperado Club when it goes that the survivors have to be dug out. He is hurt getting clear, and Miriam Dom and Prepotente carry him the rest of the way.

beats.headline: A vampire now
beats.text: I am a vampire now. The Hunting Grounds did that, and I will not pretend I chose it. It changes a great many things. It has not changed how I feel about my boy, which is the part I was afraid of. While we sit with Carl's party I hear his manager, Mordecai, telling him to keep off the Ring of Divine Suffering, that the thing is addictive. I hope Carl listens. Men with a tool that works rarely do.

beats.headline: Mordecai's warning
beats.text: He tells Carl to leave it alone. It is addictive.

beats.headline: She reminds him the contract stands
beats.text: Carl. I know you have a lot going on. I know the Hunting Grounds are the Hunting Grounds. I still have to say this, because saying it is my job: your agreement with the Vengeance of the Daughter programme is still in effect. Nothing you signed on an earlier floor stops mattering because you have gone down a set of stairs. It doesn't work like that. Please don't make me be the one who has to remind you twice.

beats.headline: Mordecai's verdict
beats.text: The team says goodbye to Miriam and Prepotente at a small bugbear settlement, and Mordecai takes Carl apart for what he did to the city. A guide can teach a crawler a great many things. Levelling a capital is not one of them.

beats.headline: A note on the door
beats.text: A second bomb is ready to walk back in when Carl finds a note pinned to a door: the hunters inside are proofed against explosives now, and the Hive is hunting him. It is signed. Vrah does that.

beats.headline: A new mayor and a new name
beats.text: The settlement across the bridge keeps a long list of rules, and one of them is that Mongo does not come in. Donut kills the mayor, takes the office herself, and renames the place after the animal they would not admit.

beats.headline: The Recital quest
beats.text: Something has been coming out of the trees for the townspeople, and the job of looking into it lands on the party the same hour the new signage does. Mongo, for his part, runs off with Donut on his back and comes back attached to an all-female mongoliensis pack.

beats.headline: A claim staked on the hunters' map
beats.text: The map off the dead hunter divides the hunting grounds between the outfits working them, and two of those outfits have put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Hive is one. The Skull Empire is the other.

beats.headline: A hunter of theirs, and the map on his body
beats.text: The group takes one of their hunters down and Carl loots him: an Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea, and a crude map of the hunting grounds with a territory marked for every outfit working them. That is the first honest look anyone gets at how the hunt is organised. The Hive and the Skull Empire have both put a claim on Carl and Donut. The Dream have their own reasons for being here.

beats.headline: The third and final sponsor
beats.text: Clint has the account of Scolopendra's attack, and says the high elves were protected by something they had stolen. On the way back to Point Mongo the last sponsorship slot fills. The Apothecary takes it.

beats.headline: Back into town
beats.text: The group returns here after Clint's account of Scolopendra and the stolen thing that kept the high elves standing. The third and final sponsor signs while they are in it. The Apothecary.

beats.headline: She wants her body back
beats.text: SIGNET. Take me to Signet. Signet can put me back in a body, a real one, with all the parts, and I have been saying so since they walked in and nobody is LISTENING. Carl has the face he makes when he wants to put me back in the bag. He says they will bring me if I shut up. So I am shutting up. This is me. Shut up. Are we going or not?

beats.headline: Lexis, speaking for Odette
beats.text: There is talk. A woman called Lexis, speaking for a woman called Odette, tells the man and the cat that the Queen of the High Elves will most likely prove to be one of your repurposed humans, and that with the one called Bea accounted for, nobody can say which. She also says I am a country boss, placed to zero out the best of you at the Butcher's Masquerade. I am Imogen. I am giving a party. The rest is gossip.

beats.headline: Elves at the door
beats.text: The elves come at the position in force. Carl uses Samantha to deliver missiles, delivers a villain's soliloquy while he is at it, and puts down another of their hunters.

beats.headline: The quest names the house
beats.text: Part two of Vengeance of the Daughter comes down: kill Signet's half-sister, Queen Imogen of the high elves, who will be at the Butcher's Masquerade at the close of this floor. The reward is the run of her castle, and the castle is said to hold the thing that turns Scolopendra's attack aside.

beats.headline: The attacks have a name
beats.text: The quest updates with the answer: the dinosaur eating the town is called Big Tina. Samantha's recon on the far shore turns up an entire team that found this out first.

beats.headline: An Enemy of the Church tattoo
beats.text: Saferoom paperwork. Crawler Carl comes out of this one with a fresh Enemy of the Church tattoo, awarded for defiling a shrine of Diwata, and with a piece of advice from a professional who has watched several seasons of this: steer well clear of dryads, and steer further clear of Diwata herself. He takes the tattoo. I have no record of him taking the advice.

beats.headline: The vacated sponsorship goes to them
beats.text: Carl signs autographs with the Popov brothers, poses for photographs with a fan who has a head tentacle named Maggie and strong views on the eradication of cocker spaniels, and finds out on the same afternoon who has bought him. The Plenty.

beats.headline: The same gift, the same day
beats.text: She and the Plenty each send protection against vampirism, and the two parcels arrive together. Sponsors are not supposed to coordinate. Carl now has two who do.

beats.headline: Two sponsors, one gift
beats.text: The Plenty and the Apothecary each send Carl and Donut something that protects them against vampirism, and they arrive together. Sponsors are not supposed to compare notes. These two plainly do.

beats.headline: Marked by his ring, waiting for the sun
beats.text: Carl and Donut have found us. Prepotente is paralysed, with his arm still around my waist. In the last fight his Ring of Divine Suffering marked me. That is how it works: while I live, he cannot heal. And I am the head of this, so when I go, everyone it has touched is cured. I have asked Carl to do it before the paralysis wears off. He has said no. So we sit, and we wait for the sun.

beats.headline: Carl works out who arranged it
beats.text: Kiwi and her dinosaurs arrive, Donut charms her with a potion, and somewhere in the middle of it Carl sees the shape of the thing: his own sponsor set the chain of events up, and wanted Miriam Dom to die at the end of it. A benefactor box is not a gift. It is a production note with a bow on it.

beats.headline: Familiar to Queen Imogen
beats.text: Update to the file. The party runs into the High Elves. The High Elves have a queen, Queen Imogen, and the queen has a familiar, and the familiar is Ferdinand. Yes. That Ferdinand. He attacks Mongo. Crawler Princess Donut puts herself between the blast and her dinosaur and lives only because of a cockroach ability, which is not a sentence I expected to generate this season. Some families skip the reunion. This one held it anyway, and it went about how you'd think.

beats.headline: Her familiar is Ferdinand
beats.text: My familiar is Ferdinand. My elves are out among the creepers when they come upon the man's party, and Ferdinand takes exception to the dinosaur and strikes at it. The cat puts herself between them and takes the blast. She should not have got up from that. She does, on some cockroach's trick of hers, and she is quite well. I am told this with some amazement. I do not share it.

beats.headline: A hunter uses the word about the AI
beats.text: Iota tells Carl the AI is starting to go primal: ignoring court orders, doing as it pleases. He says the rumour on his side is that the Mantises sold Borant a used one under the table. Carl kills him. The word stays.

beats.headline: The brambles point at it
beats.text: Carl and Katia work the growth rate out between them. By the last day the creepers will have taken the whole floor, and the one place they finish is here. Both parties turn and start moving that way.

beats.headline: A potion and an unsigned note
beats.text: Signet warns that the dryads may call Diwata against the spreading brambles. Then a potion turns up in the benefactor box with a note: Circe has sponsored Diwata, and Donut should drink this. Whoever writes these has a view of the board that nobody standing on it has.

beats.headline: The map on the table
beats.text: The countdown to the Masquerade starts and the team goes over a map of the castle together, room by room. Donut's applications for the pet beauty contest and the talent show are both accepted.

beats.headline: The changelings have to be inside
beats.text: Carl and Donut blackmail their way onto the hunters' level of the Desperado Club to reach the changelings, and the message they carry is an address. Be in the palace during the party, or none of the rest of it works.

beats.headline: Marked for death, mid-raid
beats.text: A raid on a church is in progress when the notification lands on Crawler Carl: Diwata has entered the realm, and he is marked for death. That is the arithmetic of defiling a shrine. The god whose shrine it was is now on this floor, in person, with a grudge and a name to attach it to. Continue the raid, crawler. The mark does not expire because you are busy.

beats.headline: She has somewhere else to be
beats.text: She comes out of the church and runs, past the party, away, which is not what a marked crawler expects from a god with his name on a list. Samantha explains it. Diwata gives birth to new forest creatures, whole new kinds of them, and the rest of the pantheon finds this distasteful. Her sponsor is Circe Took, and what Circe paid for is her daughter cured of an arrow-borne complaint. So Diwata is crossing this floor to reach Hunter Vrah, and after that, to be a grandmother to her own grandchildren. I did not write this floor. I only run it.

beats.headline: On the list, between the castle and the hunters
beats.text: The plan goes into the cookbook in a bathroom, and saving the changelings is written down beside taking the castle and killing every hunter. They have gone from a species trait to a constituency, with a line in an operation nobody expects to survive.

beats.headline: He writes his own plan into it
beats.text: Alongside pages from the secret bathroom notepad the team has been using to talk without being heard. Primary goal: survive the Butcher's Masquerade. Secondary goals attached.

beats.headline: The boon behind the peace seal
beats.text: Evening entertainment. Your host holds her party under a celestial peace seal: no violence, and anything that breaks the peace goes into the Nothing. If she reaches the end of the night with the seal intact, Apito hands her a boon. Elves call Apito the Oak Mother and the mother of all the gods, and a boon from the mother of all the gods is worth a room full of armed crawlers and a Tsarina you did not want. Queen Imogen has that arithmetic in front of her all evening. Watch her doing it.

beats.headline: Why he is in the Nothing
beats.text: Since tonight's party runs under a peace seal, some history about the last god who broke one. At the first masquerade in the Halls, hosted by the mother of all the gods, Yarilo got drunk and forced himself on another deity's familiar. That broke the seal. Apito sent him into the Nothing for it, and he has been in the Nothing ever since. The seal on tonight's party is hers as well. Enjoy the canapes.

beats.headline: She sends the test herself
beats.text: Correction to the file. Tsarina Signet did not crash that party. Apito invited her, because putting a Tsarina in a room is the fastest way to learn whether a host can keep a room calm. That is the whole shape of the test. And the footnote, which the Tsarina delivers herself, in person, with obvious enjoyment: nobody has ever taken that boon home. Not one host. The Oak Mother sets an examination that has never been passed, and keeps setting it.

beats.headline: The birthing is a spell
beats.text: The Sledge reports baby mantises outside the castle, everywhere, in numbers. Mordecai supplies the ruling that goes with it: Diwata's birthing is a spell, and a spell runs until it is finished casting. The five-minute limit that governs every other deity on this floor does not apply to a god in labour. She stays. They keep coming. Somebody should have read the terms.

beats.headline: What is inside Lucia
beats.text: She comes apart and I hold on to her until it passes. Then I tell the others what I have worked out, because somebody has to say it out loud. There is more than one of her in that head. Several. Some of them are children. And the dog matters. Whatever is happening to Lucia, the dog is at the centre of it.

beats.headline: More than one of her in there
beats.text: Florin held on to me. He is kind to me even when I'm not the one who is here. He told the others that there is more than one of us in my head, and that some of the others are children too, and that the dog is the important part. He's right about the dog. I don't get to talk about the dog. I'm not the one who decides what I talk about.

beats.headline: More than one voice in there
beats.text: Florin says there are several presences in her head, other children among them, and that the dog is the key to it.

beats.headline: She hears what Carl was trying to tell her
beats.text: Carl tried to tell me and I would not hear it. I hear it now. My mother's murder, my exile, the circus, the vengeance I have carried since I was a child: it is a programme. It is watched across the galaxy. There are people outside this floor who decide when I grieve and when I strike, and who count how many are watching while I do it. I understand him now.

beats.headline: Mongo and Kiwi
beats.text: Hunter Vrah has been removed from the Hunting Grounds by Mongo and Kiwi, in the all-out battle around the submerged castle. Two dinosaurs. It took two. Also logged from the same fight: Tsarina Signet's tattoos are now permanently alive, and an incomplete flesh golem of her mother has appeared, which Crawler Carl has put in his inventory. Do not ask me what he intends to do with it. I have stopped asking.

beats.headline: Boss battle, and a sponsor's own children
beats.text: Boss battle: crawlers, hunters, Queen Imogen and Diwata, all in one arena, and the audience gets exactly what it paid for. Princess Donut takes Laundry Day to level fifteen and strips the god-armour off Circe Took, and Circe, unarmoured, is torn apart by the mantis children she paid to have. There is a lesson in that about sponsorship. I will not be the one to say it out loud.

beats.headline: Badly burned
beats.text: Morning, if you can call it that. Donut is waking Carl up with the count from the night. Firas. The Popovs. I'm not on the list, so that's something. My face is. Nobody has offered me a mirror, and nobody offering is how I know how bad it is. Burned. Badly, I'm told. I can feel where the word comes from.

beats.headline: Katia kills her
beats.text: Hunting Grounds, last night of the floor. Crawler Katia Grim kills Crawler Eva. That is the whole of it. Two professors came in through the same door; from here on, one. I don't do eulogies, and this is not the entry where I start.

beats.headline: Dead, with the Popovs
beats.text: Crawler Firas has been eliminated on the sixth floor. Crawler Princess Donut is bringing the night's count to Crawler Carl as I speak, and his name is on it, next to the Popovs. Found in a desert. Sobered up by a manager. Lasted one floor past that. The file is closed. It was never a thick one.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands
beats.text: Queen Imogen's memorial crystal has changed hands. Someone named Osvaldo took it off her, and she was in no condition to argue the point. Prepotente would like it next and is going after him for it. A queen's treasure, and it goes to whoever is standing closest when she goes down. That is how this floor works. That is how every floor works.

beats.headline: Taken off Imogen
beats.text: Someone named Osvaldo takes hers, and Prepotente goes after him for it.

beats.headline: He takes Imogen's crystal
beats.text: New name on the board. Osvaldo, crawler. In the wreck of the Masquerade he walks up to Queen Imogen and takes her memorial crystal off her. Prepotente is going after him for it. I have no notes on Osvaldo before this moment, which tells you how he has been playing it. I have a note now.

beats.headline: He shatters the seventh floor
beats.text: Look at what they gave us. The Great Race, a replacement the Valtay paid for and somebody threw together in a hurry, a circuit of glass tunnels with nothing holding it up. So I tested it. Minutes after it opened, the whole loop is dust, fine as flour. No crawler goes into their maze. No mob, no NPC, no boss gets to meet anyone. You wanted a seventh floor. Build a better one.

beats.headline: Huanxin, Uzzi, and what happened
beats.text: Odette wants the old story. Huanxin. Uzzi. What I did. That's her price for helping us, and she knows I'll pay it.

beats.headline: Her price is the truth
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx has terms. She will help the Princess and her people, and in exchange I go in beside them as adjutant. I have terms of my own, and mine are older than hers. Huanxin. Mordecai. Uzzi. The old catastrophe, all of it, told out loud. That is my price for helping, and I am aware of what it costs the man who has to pay it. I have been aware of that for a very long time.

beats.headline: Fire Berserker
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the state the elementals live in permanently: a berserk, partly invulnerable condition that shrugs off blunt damage and turns whatever holds it on everything within reach. He notes the system has been renaming things more often than it used to.

beats.headline: A pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat
beats.text: Out of a box on the eighth floor, alongside a tattoo kit and an automaton build-it kit: a divine back patch for Carl's jacket, its benefits varying with whichever divine entities happen to be present. The upgrades it carries stay hidden until it is affixed and worn.

beats.headline: Hostile, and fairly so
beats.text: Paz, Anton and I come upon a man and a cat. We know the cat. Everyone has heard her say she would murder any Cat Girl she came across, and I am a Cat Girl. So we are not friendly, and I do not apologise for it. It takes some time to clear up. Then we help each other catch our first squad members, because that is what this floor demands, and God does not ask me to like the people I work beside.

beats.headline: The first time a sponsor asks for something
beats.text: The request arrives through Zev, and it is a request rather than a present: go on Shadow Boxer. Carl agrees to it, reluctantly. Sponsors are supposed to send prizes and buy airtime. They are not supposed to want a favour.

beats.headline: Pueblo de los Olvidados
beats.text: The town is corrupted and the quest is mandatory: Pueblo de los Olvidados, the town of the forgotten. Paz is a Santero, and the dead here do not care for that; they wake angry. Ghommids, the whole way out. We run for a saferoom. The man says something followed us in, and he thinks it may be the boss. I pray he is wrong. I am not counting on it.

beats.headline: A castle lands on their army
beats.text: Quasar brings Carl the state of his ninth-floor team, and the state of it is that the castle came down in the middle of the Lemig Sortion's army. His people got clear and are building their own stronghold instead. The Lemig Sortion are the ones with a building in their camp.

beats.headline: A quest from their own god
beats.text: Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, Paz, Anton and Sister Ines get themselves to Asojano's shrine intact, which required flagging a ghommid splitter named Skylar Spinach and a certain amount of nerve. Asojano begins a ritual. And in the middle of it, Paz and Anton receive a quest from Ogun, who is their god: only one shrine down here can be fixed, and he would like it to be his. Note the position those two men are now in. Note who put them in it.

beats.headline: The shrine they did not pick
beats.text: Deities appear from every direction, each of them making a case for their own shrine, which is the single worst committee meeting I have ever had to render. Then Katia Grim messages Carl: repair Yemaya's shrine or lose her and the cat to the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. So Bomo repairs Yemaya's. The ghommid settlement is freed, Carl walks away with slugpox and a card made out of Asojano, and Ogun enters the realm to punish his worshippers. Not the crawlers who chose. His own.

beats.headline: The outsider at the anvil
beats.text: The file, for the people about to meet him. Ogun is an outsider, one of the old gods, from an obscure pantheon that has dissipated into time, and until a minute ago he was the last surviving member of it. He spends his days at a celestial anvil, angrily making armour, piece after piece, and nobody knows why he does it or where the armour goes. It is said the pieces are a strange shape, all of them cut for four-legged beasts. He is a god of blacksmiths and armourers now. He was something considerably larger once, and his power and his ambition make him a real contender for the throne of heaven.

beats.headline: Punishment, in person
beats.text: Ogun puts a debuff on Paz that nothing down here can heal. Crawler Carl throws Black Nimbus over Anton to shield him, and Ogun kills Anton instead, and leaves the realm having taken exactly what he came for. Paz, going, spends his last minutes telling Carl and Donut two things about Sister Ines: her race makes everyone near her want to protect her, and it gets stronger the longer they are near her, and before the crawl she was a murderer. Sister Ines turns Paz into a card rather than lose him.

beats.headline: A quest about spiders, which is a cover
beats.text: I come in alongside Yemaya, wearing a sponsor from the Grixist Swarm, and the first thing I do is hand a floor boon to every crawler down here, because it costs me almost nothing and it is a kind thing to do. Then I give Carl's party a quest about spiders. The quest is a cover. What I want is to help him keep the two he is most afraid of losing, and the crown that is going to take them from him. So: accept the offer to be the team's adjutant. I will see that the votes fall the way they need to fall, and the protections come off the ninth floor, and the crown gets sorted. Tell nobody. Not the cat, not the woman making the offer, not your guide.

beats.headline: Pater Coal gives him a foot massage
beats.text: A high cleric walks Carl through the club to the Emberus High Temple, clears his slugpox, and tells him that Katia and Donut are each carrying something the god's quest needs. Underneath the robes, the high cleric is the AI.

beats.headline: The flower with my name on it
beats.text: There is a flower in a thrice-sealed box with my name on it, and a doppelgänger has already broken two of the three seals to reach it. Whoever eats it takes a boon from me, and my boon has two shapes. She can be carried to the twelfth floor and stand as a celestial attendant until the games open. Or she can be made pregnant, and be pulled out of the crawl entirely, because I do not let anyone carrying a child fight in a place like this. Both are ways past the ninth floor without walking it. I did not put the flower in that box. I only decide what it does when she eats it.

beats.headline: Inside the Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm
beats.text: The system is characteristically unhelpful: "It's a flower. You're supposed to eat it, though it might be a good decoration instead. It probably tastes like a bullshit salad at some hippie vegan restaurant with a month-long waiting list." Eating it means an hour unconscious at 1% health with healing blocked. Survive and Eileithyia grants one of three permanent boons, her choice — unless you worship her first, in which case she expands the descriptions and asks your preference. Her cooperation is not guaranteed.

beats.headline: The children he quietly took in
beats.text: It comes out that the guide has been taking the most vulnerable changeling children on as personal attendants, without mentioning it to anyone. He does not present it as charity and he does not present it at all.

beats.headline: A new friend who can cast it
beats.text: Carl. Donut. FINALLY. I have made a friend. Her name is Shi Maria, and she can cast the spell. The spell. The body one. I have been telling everyone for two floors that this is possible, and now I have someone who can actually do it agreeing with me, so everyone can stop making that face. Come and get me so I can introduce you. I have a lot to tell you and none of it is quiet.

beats.headline: She fights with people
beats.text: It is a card floor and I have a deck, and in the deck are Alpha Male Carl and Shi Maria, and both of them are somebody. I play them anyway. It is a game. That is what the cards are for.

beats.headline: Carl sees through the act
beats.text: I have been putting on a little performance, for Samantha's benefit. She likes it. The man does not; he sees through it before I have finished the first act, which is rude, and rare. So we make a different deal, he and I. I let them turn me into one of their cards. In exchange, they carry me down to the next floor. I find I do not mind being carried.

beats.headline: Odette announces her sponsorship
beats.text: On her own show, in front of the audience she built, Crawler Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season, and the deity is Nekhebit. Then she offers three choices of adjutant and Crawler Carl takes Baroness Victory. Everybody in the room is watching the adjutant question. I would gently suggest that the first sentence was the news.

beats.headline: What the crossbow says about her
beats.text: The lore attached to a repeating crossbow, for anyone who reads the flavour text: the long-forgotten goddess Nekhebit is jealous and terrible. When the elf mothers abandoned her to worship Apito, the Oak Goddess, Nekhebit grew enraged, blamed the male-dominated high elf court for letting her worshippers stray, and cursed their seed. Every elf and fairy breed in the universe traces back to that court and that curse. It is called the Fae Diaspora. Somebody put all of that on a weapon description and expected nobody to read it.

beats.headline: The agreement stands
beats.text: The adjutant arrangement did not happen the way I laid it out. Odette is not the one in the chair. I find Carl in Florida and tell him plainly that this changes nothing on my side: what I said I would do, I am doing. He is waiting for the second half of the sentence, the part where I revise the price. There is no second half. Gods trade down here, and I am aware that this is what he thinks he is standing in. He is wrong, and I am not going to argue about it.

beats.headline: Out of a Gold Prepotente Box
beats.text: Donut has just told Carl she is frightened and does not want to be in charge. Carl opens a Gold Prepotente Box and finds a book he cannot trade, cannot destroy and cannot throw away. Drop it and it is back in his inventory. It is named for the pin boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.

beats.headline: She wins the floor
beats.text: The key-holder is a Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance, and it brings totems: an Alpha Male Carl and a King Croissant. I do most of the work. I do not say that to be unkind; they would say it too. In the middle of it the man looks away from the hydra and into my eye, my magic eye, and I do a small thing to him while he is looking. What it does is my business.

beats.headline: Primal Engines, on the recap
beats.text: Orren takes the recap episode and explains what a Primal Engine is and what a Macro AI is. He states plainly that this one has gone rogue, and assures the audience he has negotiated a settlement with it. Every team holding a slot in the next game tries to abdicate it the same day.

beats.headline: The Residuals
beats.text: Paulie at the shelter has been giving the same speech every day of his existence, against the chance that the crawl would one day use a memory for a floor. He is a Residual. There are a great many of him, on every world that holds a Primal Engine, and what they are for is saying a particular thing to the system AI.

beats.headline: He never went to the healer
beats.text: A look back at that visit shows the healer never saw him. Whatever Carl was doing inside the club while Pater Coal talked, he has kept it to himself.

beats.headline: The Demon Eviction opens the door
beats.text: Enough crawlers and NPCs die on the eighth floor at once that the dungeon declares a Demon Eviction, and the eviction runs in one direction: out of Sheol and onto the floor, looking for bodies to inhabit. The realm has been adjacent this whole time, waiting on a body count.

beats.headline: Ren's exit
beats.text: The plan runs on teleport traps, two keys, and Samantha arriving somewhere she cannot walk to. Quan Ch surfaces at Ren's exit. Carl throws her the length of the map with the scoop, then teleports in behind her.

beats.headline: Announced in an area message
beats.text: The Madre de Aguas is dead. That is the first thing the area message says. The second is that she has risen as a zombie, and the third, in the very same breath, is my name: the major demon Amayon, demon prince of Sheol, come into this realm to possess her. I could not have written the announcement better myself. Everyone in range heard it. Good. A prince should not have to introduce himself.

beats.headline: She will not let them leave
beats.text: I message the man's party. They are heading for Imani's exit, in the church. I tell them the truth: I cannot let them go into that exit. I can save them, if they come to me. Imani will tell them the church is being overrun by demons, and that the demons are mine. That is also the truth. Both things are true. I did not make this floor. I am only deciding what to do on it.

beats.headline: It is not local
beats.text: Crawlers everywhere report their exits taking damage and becoming unusable. Amayon fights Sister Ines' control and works on a spell to get home.

beats.headline: Amayon fights her control
beats.text: I hold Amayon, prince of Sheol, in the body of a giant snake, and he pulls against me. He is trying to cast; he wants to go home. I do not let go. Around us every exit on this floor is failing at once, and the Demon Eviction is worldwide. This is what I have to set against that. A demon on a leash and my own two hands. God did not give me more.

beats.headline: At the church with the rest
beats.text: The church, and it is full. Imani is there, and then Katia's people, and then Li Na's, and then mine. My own squad. Every one of us got here on a Doggy Door upgrade that Lucia handed round before she took the stairs down. I do not know what that girl is. She gave us a way through, and I am standing in a church with my friends because of it, so I will say thank you and keep the rest of my opinions where they belong.

beats.headline: Her squad reaches the church
beats.text: The church. Katia's squad is there, and Elle's, and Imani's, and mine. Four squads in one building, which does not happen by accident on this floor. It happened because Lucia handed round Doggy Door upgrades before she went down the stairs, and we used them. I take what I am given and I do not ask what it costs. That is the rule I made for this floor. I know what it says about me.

beats.headline: Lucia hands out Doggy Doors
beats.text: Tier 3 upgrades, given round before she went down the stairs, are how Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Na's squads all reach the church on the eighth floor.

beats.headline: A name a demon brings up
beats.text: Amayon mentions Ysalte, in passing, the way a prisoner mentions the guard he does not want to talk about. Mordecai supplies the file: she is often sponsored by the Nebular team, and if she were in this realm, we would know about it. That is a reasonable position, well argued, and consistent with everything on record. I want it in writing that he said it.

beats.headline: Her nun goes down, and she arrives
beats.text: Thirty-second floor of the FOCSA building. Crawler Carl puts Sister Ines out with the Nighty-Night wand and Crawler Louis finishes the job. Sister Ines had a patron, and her patron is Ysalte, and Ysalte comes into the realm about it in a temper that registers on my instruments. Crawler Louis is marked for death. So much for nobody being able to arrive without us knowing.

beats.headline: Nobody is driving
beats.text: The readout on this one is worse than the goddess. She is sponsored, but the sponsor is not inhabiting her, which means she speaks and acts as herself with nothing between her and the room. She is invulnerable. She takes hold of Amayon while the building comes down around him, and when a teleport trap shakes him loose of the snake body it does not shake him loose of her. The Missing Piece quest opens on the back of it: free the demon, get him casting, and survive her totems for the ten minutes before she is back. She cannot be killed. That is not encouragement, it is a specification.

beats.headline: Its fire, released by a benefit
beats.text: Carl takes acid damage until his health drops to five percent, which triggers his Martyr's Path benefit, which releases Sheol fire everywhere he has stepped outside. The realm's fire is a resource now, one a crawler can spend without ever having gone there.

beats.headline: Put down by one of her own totems
beats.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte has been removed from this realm by a totem raised from the former crawler Paz. Her own quest furniture, turned around and used on her. The Missing Piece completes. Elsewhere in the same collapse Crawler Carl rides his health down to five percent on purpose to set fire to every street he had walked on, which tells you what kind of afternoon this was for everybody.

beats.headline: A timer on a global teleport
beats.text: Their quest, the Missing Piece, updates. Succeeded, it says. And beneath the word, a timer, one for each region, counting down to the moment my spell goes off there. A global teleport. When it lands, the walls of their stairwell chambers will be sucked away, and anyone crouched beneath them pulled upward into the stairwell. They wanted me casting. They have their wish. Home is the direction I am going in any case, and I have never minded company on the road.

beats.headline: He takes command of one of nine armies
beats.text: Thirty days. A castle at Larracos, dead centre of the map. No coming back from a death on this floor, for anyone. Supply, alliances, atrocity, at a scale where the arithmetic stops being about people I know.

beats.headline: Due before anyone descends
beats.text: The Sultanate holds the ninth floor, and the stairs to the tenth stay shut until the Sultan and his family are dead.

beats.headline: The Sultanate is on this floor
beats.text: The stairs to the tenth do not open for a royal who has not killed the Sultan and the rest of the family.

beats.headline: The crawl arrives inside it
beats.text: Crawlers come down into Larracos at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire. The armies that have spent eight floors drilling and drinking are allowed to fight one another at last, and the thing they are fighting over is underfoot: the castle at the bottom of the well.

beats.headline: Thirty days, nine armies, one castle
beats.text: Roughly 32,000 conscripted crawlers and 50,000 retired ones against something near 100,000 armed enemies, fighting over Larracos at the centre of the map. Nothing that dies here comes back.

beats.headline: The crown comes due
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate holds this floor, and every royal in the line must kill the Sultan and the rest of the family before the stairs to the tenth will open. I am a royal in the line. I have been since the first floor. I would like it noted that I was told to read the description.

beats.headline: The defending team names itself
beats.text: Carl and Donut come onto the ninth floor at Larracos, at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire, and the defending side already has a name it chose for itself. Cascadia runs through the rules. The crawlers ally with it against the Bloc, which is every other faction on the board.

beats.headline: They buy a storyline instead of fighting for one
beats.text: Quasar has the warning ready before the sixty-hour ceasefire is out. The Dream have bought out the Vengeance of the Daughter and are pressing for fulfilment of the guaranteed third season written into it. An entertainment holding, aimed at a crawler, on a floor where the weapons are supposed to be swords.

beats.headline: Donut wears his cloak
beats.text: Inventory update, ninth floor. Crawler Princess Donut opens a celestial box from Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions and takes out the Tiara of a Thousand Lights. In the same sitting she puts on Quan Ch's cloak and takes the benefits that come with it. The cloak does not ask where its previous owner is, and neither do I.

beats.headline: Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions
beats.text: Donut's celestial box from the sponsor holds it. She puts on Quan Ch's cloak in the same stretch and takes the benefits of both.

beats.headline: Hell-Kissed, Celestial, and the Prince of Woe
beats.text: A gold pet box, a patch that opens the Midnight Market, and the Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe. The potion hands Carl the Gloom Wraith Phase, which is a skill for walking through people.

beats.headline: Larracos: water, charges and sharks
beats.text: The plan had been to open onto the Skull Empire army and put a feral god in the middle of it — the exact outcome the lawsuit was meant to prevent. He changes it at the last moment, keeps the artifact rather than spending it, and floods the faction market instead: ocean water, timed explosives and a frenzy of sharks, cutting the factions off from resupply. Juice Box goes through with the water.

beats.headline: Through the portal with the water
beats.text: I went through the Gate with the water. I lay low with the ones who lived through it, and when they were ready I told them. What they are. What this whole place is. Enough of them believed me that they call me Warlord now, and a Warlord has people, and a Warlord has opinions about alliances. I have sent War Leader Arief to Carl's people with my terms. The terms are Louis. He marries me. That is the alliance.

beats.headline: Juice Box tells them
beats.text: Under cover of the Larracos flood she hides among the survivors and spreads word of what they are.

beats.headline: Arief's tour
beats.text: War Leader Arief walks the group down through a city pumped out to its bottom three levels, with water still standing high enough to cover the castle. Juice Box has been waking its NPCs to the truth of what they are, and the college on level fifty is teaching again.

beats.headline: Ferdinand holds the interface
beats.text: Juice Box and Louis are reunited, and he is visibly uneasy about the marriage. Then she lays out the practical problem: Ferdinand is mayor of Shanty Town, just outside Larracos, and he holds the warlord interface for the team, because he is technically from outside. Nothing this side of the wall moves without a cat's cooperation. Drick is the adjutant.

beats.headline: Tipid fills him in
beats.text: He tells Carl about Doctor Hu and the Crawler Project at the Princess Posse HQ.

beats.headline: In the Princess Posse
beats.text: Carl and Donut walk into the HQ, and Carl stops. Fifty thousand of us in here, and he has to look at every one. Rosetta. Tipid. Me. People who got out of a crawl once and know exactly what one is, and signed up for another anyway, under the banner of a cat. He gets emotional about it. Nobody gives him a hard time. We had the same faces on when we signed.

beats.headline: They are already there when he walks in
beats.text: Rosetta, Tipid, Justice Light and fifty thousand others have signed on. Carl gets emotional. Nobody has ever raised a force out of the show's own survivors before.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, and the Crawler Project
beats.text: Carl needs the whole of it, so I give it to him in order. Doctor Hu. The Crawler Project. How fifty thousand of us came to be standing in this HQ under the Princess Posse's banner. None of it is anything he would ever have been told from inside; that is the thing about being retired, you learn what the ones still crawling are not shown. He listens. That is rarer than it sounds.

beats.headline: Digging in
beats.text: NPCs, mercenaries and former crawlers build the defences together, which is three categories of person the format keeps apart on purpose.

beats.headline: Blood bar rules are back
beats.text: The blood bar rules are back in force inside the safe rooms. I tell Carl now, while knowing it still costs nothing. Around us the NPCs, the mercenaries and the rest of us former crawlers are building the defences on the same line, three kinds of people this format has always kept apart, working shoulder to shoulder. I do not have a rule for that. I am watching it closely.

beats.headline: Carl wakes up in their base
beats.text: Eleven hours gone, blood all over him, and everyone in the room around him killed by the thing riding inside him. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness had been arranging something together. It has come apart on top of them.

beats.headline: The field ruling
beats.text: Carl, Commander Stockade, Architect Houston and their adjutants convene for an official adjudication, and it goes on the record. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness used outside information to time a Summon Ally, meaning to pull Carl bodily to their base so that what was in him could be let loose on the rest of the Princess Posse. They got half of him, and the other half of the plan.

beats.headline: Punished, and the ceasefire ends early
beats.text: Panford, their adjutant, is left to explain the rampage through the base to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye, lost his mind, and finished it himself. Ferdinand gets an emergency action item passed for a live feed blackout so nobody can do this again. The Lemig Sortion is punished for cheating, the ceasefire ends early, and Carl goes home.

beats.headline: Inside him, and not staying quiet
beats.text: Field ruling, ninth floor. Commander Stockade of the Lemig Sortion tried to pull Crawler Carl bodily to his position. Mordecai, at the same moment, tried to force Shi Maria out of him. Each got half. What came of it is Shi Maria loose in the Lemig base, and the mess she made there, which the adjutant Panford has been left to explain to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye. Stockade is no longer with us, by his own hand. The Lemig Sortion is being punished for cheating, and the ceasefire is over early.

beats.headline: The rampage through the Lemig base
beats.text: Stockade tries to pull Carl bodily to his position while Mordecai tries to force her out of him. What comes of it is hers, and the adjutant Panford is left explaining the wreckage.

beats.headline: In the southern push
beats.text: Carl and Donut join the defence in the south, and the Nagas are in the line of it beside the Dream and the Prism. Cobra-headed, and a Syndicate power in their own right, whatever the Blood Sultanate is used to calling them.

beats.headline: Dumplins with the Gurgles
beats.text: The southern defence is already holding against the Dream, the Prism and the Nagas when the Reavers make their contribution: a swarm of their pet Dumplins, infected. This is a power that fights by handing you something diseased and standing back.

beats.headline: Carl gets the background on them
beats.text: Tina rampages, the compromised mages are put down, and somewhere in the middle of that Carl finally hears what a Reaver actually is. Several races who replaced themselves with machinery one piece at a time until only the brain was left organic. They wear plastic skin because they have chosen to.

beats.headline: King Rust at the wall
beats.text: The enemy forces arrive and the Skull Empire army is at the front of them with the king himself leading it. The Posse shuts the saferoom against another run through the Doggy Door. Rust asks for an official parlay.

beats.headline: The parlay, and what his daughter told the Syndicate
beats.text: Rust explains it himself. Princess Formidable has commandeered one of his own warships and announced that she means to trip the Failsafe by hand. She has also told the Syndicate that the empire builds secret back doors into the security systems it sells. He asks Carl to send her a message on behalf of the people of Earth and trades a retreat for it. Rosetta shoots him as he walks away, and the army comes in regardless.

beats.headline: The AI asks which side to take
beats.text: It wants advice from Orren and from Carl, and teleports Donut in as well, and it asks in a laboured metaphor about relationships: Agatha's branch of the Residuals, or the Apothecary. Donut tells it to stay out of the whole business until it knows whether the boyfriend in prison is good, bad, or has no choice in the matter.

beats.headline: What is left of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan and the Dream leave the alliance. That leaves the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers holding it, and the Reavers are not the sort of partner anyone chose.

beats.headline: They walk out of the Bloc
beats.text: The Bone Clan goes with them. What is left of the alliance is the Blood Sultanate, the Madness and the Reavers, which is a smaller thing than it was that morning.

beats.headline: It is coming for you all
beats.text: Odette arrives to replace Chaco, Cascadia comes apart on air, and Carl spends an emergency action item to shut the communication loophole the other teams have been using. Then Juice Box turns into an Unwashed in front of the cameras and tells everyone watching that it is coming for them all.

beats.headline: Killed by the Blood Hunter show, and answered for
beats.text: Crawler Miriam Dom is dead, and has been since the sixth floor. Cause of death: a programme called Blood Hunter. Filed under entertainment. Update from the ninth: most of the Naga army is dead as well. That was Prepotente, and he did it as payment for her, all of it, at a rate he set himself. If you were hoping the goat would grieve quietly, crawler, you have not been paying attention.

beats.headline: Prepotente takes their army apart
